'''Nick Young''' (born {{birth date|1985|6|1}}) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who played for the [[University of Southern California]] from [[2004 in basketball|2004]] to [[2007 in basketball|2007]]. Following his junior season, he announced that he would forgo his senior year to turn professional and enter the [[NBA Draft]]. He plays both [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions.

==College career==
Young was first team all-[[Pacific Ten Conference|Pac-10]] in 2005-2006 and 2006-2007. In the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA Tournament]], he led the fifth-seeded Trojans to a berth in the Sweet Sixteen, where they lost to the one-seeded [[North Carolina Tar Heels]], 74-64. Along the way, Young led USC to a first-round win against Arkansas. In the 2nd round, Young led the team over the [[Texas Longhorns]] in a 87-68 rout of the team featuring the nation's top player, [[Kevin Durant]].

On [[April 15]], the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' reported that Young was going to declare for the [[2007 NBA Draft]].

==High school career==
Young attended [[Cleveland High School (Los Angeles, California)|Cleveland High School]] in [[Reseda, Los Angeles, California|Reseda, California]].

==Trivia==
Young flunked out of two high schools before finally being admitted to a third (Cleveland High) out in suburban Reseda.<ref>http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/n/a/2007/06/25/sports/s122146D80.DTL</ref> 

In 1991, Young's oldest brother, Charles Jr., was murdered in a park shooting. Nick was five at the time.

Nick Young is also the main subject of a documentary titled ''Second Chance Season'', in which his exploits, short-comings, and ulterior success is reviewed by the [[Biopic|biopic]]'s [[Director|director]], Daniel H. Forer.<ref>http://movies.yahoo.com/movie/1809884053/info</ref>
